role: Async-signal-safe fatal-signal handler for the iOS app: on SIGABRT/SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGFPE/SIGILL/SIGTRAP writes a raw-address crash log to the path given at install (CrashLogManager.crashLogURL = <app group container>/crash_log.txt), then re-raises with default disposition. Compiled into the iOS app target (project.pbxproj:4150).
state: mem:g_crash_path (static char[PATH_MAX], crash file path copy)
mem:g_code_image_base / g_code_image_name / g_code_image_name_len (dladdr result for the image containing app code)
file:crash_log.txt (path passed in by CrashLogManager.installSignalHandlers, CrashLogManager.swift:457)
toplevel: Static globals lines 18-26; kFatalSignals lines 28-35 (SIGABRT,SIGSEGV,SIGBUS,SIGFPE,SIGILL,SIGTRAP) and count line 37; macro safe_write_lit (line 58) writes a string literal with compile-time length.

flags.text: The sigaction installs the handler with sa_flags=0 and no alternate signal stack (no sigaltstack/SA_ONSTACK anywhere in Emuqu/). A SIGSEGV/SIGBUS from stack overflow (e.g. runaway recursion) cannot run the handler on the exhausted stack, so the process dies with no crash_log.txt written for exactly that crash class.

units.does: Writes `count` bytes to fd with write(2), looping on short writes and retrying on EINTR; stops silently on any other error or zero-byte write.

branches.effect: loop continues writing; exits when all bytes written
retry same write; otherwise (n==0 or other error) break and abandon the remaining bytes

units.does: Renders `value` as fixed-width 0x-prefixed 16-digit lowercase hex plus newline into a 19-byte stack buffer and writes it via safe_write.

branches.effect: emit one nibble per iteration, most significant first

units.does: Renders an int as decimal into a 12-byte stack buffer back-to-front and writes it; writes "0" for zero and prefixes "-" for negatives (only signal numbers are passed in practice).

branches.effect: magnitude taken as -value (undefined for INT_MIN; never reached with signal numbers); else value

units.does: Writes the constant name of a fatal signal (SIGABRT/SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGFPE/SIGILL/SIGTRAP) or "SIGNAL" for anything else.

Fatal-signal handler: if already handling, _exit(128+sig); else sets g_handling, opens g_crash_path O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC 0600 and writes header (signal name/number, main executable slide, app code image name and load address), a symbolication how-to, raw backtrace() return addresses (max 128) and an end marker; then restores SIG_DFL and re-raises so the OS crash report is still produced. Read on next launch by CrashLogManager.promoteCurrentCrashLog (CrashLogManager.swift:424) into previous_crash.txt.
units.entry: Installed via sigaction for the six kFatalSignals by emuqu_install_crash_signal_handlers; invoked by the kernel on the crashing thread.

branches.cond: g_handling already set (a fatal signal arrived during handling, or a second thread crashed concurrently)
branches.effect: _exit(128+signal_number) immediately, no log, no OS re-raise; otherwise continue
write the full log and close; if open fails (e.g. container unavailable) nothing is written and the handler goes straight to re-raise

flags.text: Calls backtrace() from signal context; backtrace is not on the POSIX async-signal-safe list. The installer pre-warms it (line 217) to reduce, not eliminate, the risk of lazy initialisation inside the handler.

The re-entrancy guard is process-wide, but sa_mask is empty and only the handled signal is blocked on the handling thread, so a fatal signal on a SECOND thread while the first is still writing hits g_handling and calls _exit(128+sig): the process ends mid-write, leaving a truncated crash_log.txt (no END OF CRASH LOG) and no OS crash report because the signal is never re-raised. The comment justifying the guard assumes the second signal comes from the handler itself.

units.does: Copies crash_file_path into g_crash_path, records main-executable slide (_dyld_get_image_vmaddr_slide(0)) and, via dladdr on itself, the base name and load address of the image holding app code (Emuqu.debug.dylib on Xcode debug builds), warms backtrace(), then installs emuqu_signal_handler with sigaction for the six fatal signals. Returns false on NULL/empty/over-long path or the first sigaction failure. Called from CrashLogManager.installSignalHandlers (CrashLogManager.swift:457), which NSLogs on false.

branches.effect: return false, no handlers installed; else copy path
store dli_fbase and base name of dli_fname ("" if dli_fname NULL), truncated to 255 chars; else store "(dladdr failed)" and leave g_code_image_base NULL (logged as 0x0)
take substring after last slash; else whole path
return false immediately; handlers already installed for earlier signals stay installed (partial install reported as total failure)

flags.text: A sigaction failure on signal k returns false with handlers for signals 0..k-1 left installed; CrashLogManager.installSignalHandlers then logs "failed to install signal handlers", which misstates a partial install as none.
